subject.title: fix(codex): coalesce in-flight dynamic tool calls

question: Should OpenClaw treat two Codex dynamic-tool requests with different `callId` values but identical same-turn payloads as one idempotent operation, or preserve them as distinct executions absent an upstream retry-delivery guarantee?
rationale: The patch intentionally changes the operation identity boundary, and current review evidence does not establish that the upstream protocol authorizes payload-based deduplication across distinct call IDs.

options.title: Preserve call-ID identity
options.body: Keep one execution per `callId` and pursue duplicate suppression only through an upstream-supported retry or idempotency signal.

options.title: Adopt payload coalescing
options.body: Accept same-turn matching payloads as one operation, document the compatibility contract, and add focused coverage for observer, audit, and side-effect semantics across both IDs.

recommendation.title: Preserve call-ID identity
recommendation.body: Keep one execution per `callId` and pursue duplicate suppression only through an upstream-supported retry or idempotency signal.

likelyOwner.reason: A Codex runtime-area owner must confirm the operation-identity contract; available evidence cannot safely name an individual.
